transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I’m here because I keep not finishing things all the way at work. Like sanitation steps, batch logs, end-of-line paperwork… I start them, but I’ll miss the last parts somehow, even though I know it really matters for my job.
Have you noticed this kind of difficulty finishing tasks all the way through since you were a kid, or is this something that's really started more recently?

I think it goes back pretty far. My mom has some old report cards, like from fourth grade, that say I was bright but needed a lot of reminders to finish classwork and turn homework in. I remember getting the lessons, but if the teacher wasn’t kind of right there, I’d miss parts of the instructions.
When you leave a step unfinished, is it usually because your attention drifted elsewhere, or because you feel a strong urge to check or redo something until it feels 'right'?

It’s more like my attention drifts. I’m not really trying to redo it until it feels right. Even if I start the shift really focused, after a while the cutting and weighing and labels kind of blur together, and then I’ll notice I’m just staring at the same tray or the log sheet and not really taking in what I’m supposed to do next.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or noticing you've lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?
Um… not really, I don’t think so. I mean, I get frustrated, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been depressed or lost interest in things.
Do you notice this same kind of difficulty finishing tasks or staying focused in other parts of your life, like at home or when you're doing personal projects, not just at work?

Mostly it’s at work. That’s what pushed me to come in. I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch logs, or the end-of-line paperwork, and somehow I leave off the last part… even though I know it has to be done right.

Thinking about things like paying bills, doing chores, or following through on personal projects at home—do you ever notice yourself losing track partway through those tasks the same way you do at work?

I don’t really notice it as much at home. The main thing is work… like I’ll start the sanitation steps or the batch logs, and then somehow the last parts don’t get done, even though I know they have to be.
When you're doing something you find really interesting or enjoyable, like a hobby or a video game, do you notice you can stay focused on that all the way through without your attention drifting?

I mean… even if I’m trying to focus, it doesn’t always stay that way. After a while, like with cutting or weighing or checking labels, it kind of all blends together, and I’ll realize I’m just staring at the tray or the log sheet without really knowing what I’m supposed to do next.
Do you notice a similar kind of drifting or losing track of details when you're in conversations or meetings with other people, even outside of work tasks?

Yeah… sometimes. Like if my supervisor is telling me something face-to-face, I’ll nod like I got it, but then a minute later I only really remember the first part. Then I have to ask someone what she just said.

Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or like you need to be moving—tapping your foot, getting up frequently, or feeling like you can't sit still for long periods, especially during tasks like paperwork or meetings?
Not really… I mean, I might shift around sometimes, but I don’t think that’s a big thing for me. It’s more like I just kind of lose track mentally, I guess.
Do you often find yourself forgetting appointments, misplacing everyday items like keys or your phone, or forgetting to do routine tasks outside of work?

Yeah… mostly at work. I’m always losing stuff I need on the floor, like my cut glove or marker, my badge, safety glasses. I’ll be sure I just had it in my hand, and then I’m walking back around for ten minutes trying to figure out where I put it.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others when they're speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations or lines?
No… I don’t think so. I’m usually not the one jumping in or anything. I might just stay quiet until it’s my turn.
